title: Named in a federal prosecution release, then paid or hired by the City
question: Which City contractors had an officer or owner charged or convicted by the U.S. Attorney, and what did the City pay and award afterwards?
finding: 2,293 federal press releases since 2015 were searched for the names of City payees and contract-team members. 4 firms are tied to a release by an officer or owner who was charged or convicted, and were paid by the City or joined a new City contract team afterwards; 1 more is named in a headline about a charge, conviction or settlement. Empire Engineering & Construction Inc: its president was charged on 7 April 2017 and convicted on 20 February 2019 in a scheme to submit rigged bids for a federal building contract; the federal exclusion list shows the firm suspended since 6 November 2017 (SBA, "Ineligible (Proceedings Pending)", no end date). In the fiscal years after the charge the City paid it $7.8 million and it joined 8 new contract teams ($5.9 million agreed); 5 of those began after the federal suspension ($4.6 million). It is in none of the City's twelve debarment reports on disk. Townsend Management Inc: a vice president was charged in the same release and convicted on 20 February 2019; in later fiscal years the City paid the firm $5.6 million and its joint venture TMI/CMP JV $10.7 million. The State licence file says of that person: left State licence 861127 on 22 October 2018.
how: The full text of every press release of the U.S. Attorney for the Northern District of California since 2015, and of the Justice Department's civil settlements for the Bay Area, is searched for the exact normalised names of City payees (paid $50,000 or more since fiscal 2019) and contract-team members. A firm is kept when the sentence gives a person's post at the firm ("President of", "owns", "her company") or the firm is in the headline, and when the City paid it $10,000 or more in fiscal years after the release or it joined a contract team that began after the release date. The latest stage is taken from later releases that name the same defendant. Public bodies, banks and airlines are left out. The join column says what second record confirms the name.
limits: A charge is an accusation; a release records one moment and later outcomes (acquittal, reversal on appeal, sentence) are often not announced, and none of the sentences in the Empire and Townsend matter is on disk. A conviction of an officer is not a conviction of the firm. Federal suspension bars federal awards and federally funded work; the City's own debarment needs its own proceeding under the Administrative Code. Payments after a charge can be for contracts won earlier, and low-bid public works must go to the lowest responsible bidder unless the City finds otherwise. A firm in a headline may be a victim or a settling party with no finding against it.
